summary: Provides a road map of the LDAP technical specification, a set of documents on accessing distributed directory services built on X.500 data and service models. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4510 is a road map for the LDAP version 3 technical specification. It names the companion RFCs and explains which earlier documents the revised suite replaces.

questions: what is the ldap technical specification
how does ldap relate to x.500
subtitle: A guide to the documents that together define the LDAP version 3 technical specification.

tldr.problem: The LDAP version 3 specification was distributed across documents that had been revised and reorganized, making it unclear which texts formed the current technical specification.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4510 lists the companion documents and describes how the suite relates to X.500 and to the earlier LDAP RFCs.
tldr.outcome: The revised LDAP suite consists of this road map and nine companion RFCs. RFC 4510 obsoletes RFC 3377 and nine earlier LDAP RFCs.

today: RFC 4510 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 3377 and the earlier LDAP specifications listed in its header. No later RFC is recorded as updating or obsoleting RFC 4510.

sections.title: The LDAP Technical Specification
sections.content:
The Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) is an Internet protocol for accessing distributed directory services that follow X.500 data and service models. RFC 4510 is a road map; the protocol itself is defined in the companion documents it lists.

The LDAP version 3 technical specification consists of this RFC and nine others. They cover the protocol, directory information models, authentication and security, distinguished names, search filters, LDAP URLs, syntaxes and matching rules, internationalized strings, and the user-application schema.

In other documents, “LDAP” and “LDAPv3” are informal names for the protocol defined by this technical specification. The suite should be identified formally by a normative reference to RFC 4510.
sections.plainLanguage: This document is the index to the LDAP version 3 specification. It points to the companion RFC for each major part of the protocol.

sections.title: The Nine Companion RFCs
sections.content:
RFC 4511 defines the LDAP protocol, and RFC 4512 defines directory information models. Authentication methods and security mechanisms are in RFC 4513. RFCs 4514, 4515, and 4516 define string formats for distinguished names and search filters, and the LDAP URL.

RFC 4517 covers syntaxes and matching rules, RFC 4518 covers internationalized string preparation, and RFC 4519 defines the schema for user applications. RFC 4518 is new to this revision; the other documents revise earlier parts of the suite.
sections.plainLanguage: Each companion RFC covers a separate topic, such as messages, names, security, or schema. Read the document for the topic you need, and use the suite together for the full specification.

sections.title: How LDAP Relates to X.500
sections.content:
The technical specification defines LDAP as an X.500 access mechanism. An LDAP server must follow the X.500 (1993) recommendations when it provides the service, but it does not have to use X.500 protocols internally.

LDAP may be mapped onto another directory system as long as the X.500 data and service models used by LDAP are preserved at the LDAP interface. The specification incorporates parts of X.500(93); later revisions of X.500 do not automatically apply.
sections.plainLanguage: An LDAP server may use different internal technology, but it must present the data and service behavior required by X.500 (1993). Newer X.500 revisions do not automatically change this specification.

sections.title: Earlier LDAP Specifications Replaced
sections.content:
RFC 4510 obsoletes the previous technical specification in RFC 3377, which consisted of RFCs 2251 through 2256, 2829, 2830, and 3771, as well as RFC 3377 itself. The suite was reorganized, and RFC 4510 replaces RFC 3377 and a section of RFC 2251.

The companion RFCs replace portions or all of the earlier protocol documents. RFC 4511 replaces most of RFC 2251, parts of RFC 2252, and all of RFC 3771. RFC 4513 replaces RFC 2829 and RFC 2830; RFCs 4514, 4515, and 4516 replace RFCs 2253, 2254, and 2255 respectively.

Each companion document includes appendices describing changes to the material it replaces.
sections.plainLanguage: The new suite replaces the earlier collection of LDAP RFCs and redistributes their material. Each companion document explains its own changes.

sections.title: Optional LDAP Extensions
sections.content:
LDAP can be extended by other documents. Extensions are expected to be truly optional, so that the base protocol remains available without them. RFC 4521's considerations for LDAP extensions apply to this revision, as do the IANA considerations in RFC 4520.

This road map does not define a name for combinations of LDAP and extensions; it notes that a future document may do so.
sections.plainLanguage: Other documents can add LDAP features, but those extensions are expected to remain optional. This road map does not define a special name for LDAP combined with extensions.

sections.title: Where LDAP Security Is Specified
sections.content:
RFC 4510 adds no security rules of its own. It states that LDAP security considerations are discussed in each document that makes up the technical specification.

RFC 4513 is the suite document on authentication methods and security mechanisms, so it is the relevant companion for those topics.
sections.plainLanguage: Security details are in the companion RFCs, not in this road map. RFC 4513 covers authentication methods and security mechanisms.
